mechanism: handle-tx (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1816-1953) calls tx-request-received on the arriving transaction's txid and, when it differs, its wtxid at :1845-1851 -- before any validation, and regardless of whether this peer was ever an announcer. tx-request-received (src/networking/protocol.lisp:463-475) is Core's ForgetTxHash: it clears *tx-in-flight* and deletes EVERY peer's announcement of the hash. Core's ReceivedTx (refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:505-513) instead calls m_txrequest.ReceivedResponse(nodeid, txid/wtxid), which MakeCompleted's only the delivering peer's announcement (refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:671-679); every other announcer stays CANDIDATE. Core reserves ForgetTxHash for genuine resolution -- MempoolAcceptedTx (:327-328), orphan intake and rejected-parents (:419-420, :434-435), BlockConnected (:107-108) -- and on a rejection forgets only the WTXID (:470), adding the txid only when the failure is TX_INPUTS_NOT_STANDARD, which by construction does not depend on the witness (:483-484).
consequence: Announcements keyed by TXID -- orphan-parent fetches (request-orphan-parents, src/networking/protocol.lisp:1638) and announcements from non-wtxidrelay peers -- can be evicted by any peer that sends an unsolicited WITNESS-MALLEATED copy of the transaction: same txid, different wtxid. The twin fails validation and is cached under its own wtxid only, so the real transaction is not blacklisted, but every honest announcer of it has been forgotten and the scheduler issues no further request. The orphan whose parent was being fetched is not resolved until an entirely new peer announces the hash. The lever costs one tx message per eviction (tx rate bucket 10/s sustained, burst 50) and is repeatable with a fresh witness each round. It is a censorship lever, not memory growth or a crash, so S2 rather than S1. Wtxid-keyed announcements are unaffected, as the finder states.
evidence: Probes in the project container (warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, worktree bl-ga11v-txrelay-s2), driven through the shipped dispatch entry point bl.net:handle-message, not the handler. (1) ga11-p1-mechanism: three peers announce one TXID, a fourth delivers a witness-malleated twin (450,000-byte witness, so it is rejected as tx-weight-too-large) -> (:IDS (:SAME-TXID T :DIFF-WTXID T) :BEFORE (:ANNOUNCERS 3 :IN-FLIGHT T :COUNTS (1 1 1)) :AFTER (:ANNOUNCERS 0 :IN-FLIGHT NIL :COUNTS (0 0 0)) :TWIN-IN-MEMPOOL NIL :REAL-PARENT-IN-MEMPOOL NIL :TXID-IN-REJECTS NIL :TWIN-WTXID-IN-REJECTS T :REQUESTS-NEXT-PASS 0). (2) Positive control ga11-p1-control: the same transaction without the malleation is accepted -> (:HONEST-IN-MEMPOOL T), so the rejection is caused by the malleation and not by the fixture. (3) ga11-p1-wtxid-entries-survive: a wtxid-keyed announcement of the honest witness transaction and a txid-keyed one of the same transaction -> (:BEFORE (:WTXID 1 :TXID 1) :AFTER (:WTXID 1 :TXID 0)). (4) ga11-p1-repeatable: 20 rounds with a fresh witness each time -> (:ROUNDS 20 :WIPES 20 :TXID-STILL-REQUESTABLE-BY-A-NEW-INV T). Ours: src/networking/protocol.lisp:411-425 (%tx-request-drop-announcer), :463-475 (tx-request-received), :1845-1851 (the two calls in handle-tx), :1563-1573 (%cache-tx-rejection caches the wtxid only). Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txdownloadman_impl.cpp:505-513, :440-490; refs/bitcoin/src/txrequest.cpp:560-566, :671-679.
fix_shape: Split the one function into Core's two. Add a per-(peer,hash) tx-request-received-response that completes only the delivering peer's announcement, and call it from handle-tx in place of the two ForgetTxHash calls; keep tx-request-received (ForgetTxHash) for the points where the transaction is genuinely resolved -- mempool acceptance in %after-mempool-accept, the orphan-intake and rejected-parents branches, the cached-rejection branch, and note-block-connected -- mirroring txdownloadman_impl.cpp:327-328, :419-420, :434-435, :470, :483 and :107-108. The rejection path must forget the WTXID only, and the TXID additionally only for the txid-determined failure class Core names (TX_INPUTS_NOT_STANDARD, our :nonstandard-inputs), which is already the rule %cache-tx-rejection follows for the rejects filter, so the two can share one predicate. This depends on announcements carrying a COMPLETED state rather than being deleted, which is finding 931a5184's fix; done together, an unsolicited or malleated delivery completes at most the sender's slot and the next scheduler pass re-routes to an honest announcer.
